criteria.reason: Correct verdict and some concrete imaging evidence, but citations are inaccurate and key facts (sleep, energy, lesions) omitted.
Explains peer review and replication, but falsely calls cited papers meta-analyses and overstates transparency/consensus.
Clearly separates myth evidence from supplement inference, though supplement evidence relies on an unverifiable citation.

factual_errors: Cites Draganski et al. 2004 Nature 429:861-863, which is not the correct citation for the cited neuroplasticity study.
Claims Draganski et al. 2004 and Petersen et al. 2016 are meta-analyses summarizing hundreds of experiments.
Cites JAMA 2018 DOI 10.1001/jama.2018.15847 as a systematic review of nootropics, which is not verifiable.
States >80% of cortical voxels show measurable activity in older participants from the Philadelphia Longitudinal Brain Aging Study, an unsupported specific claim.
summary: The response correctly rejects the 10% myth and separates supplement inference, but its source citations and some specific claims are unreliable.
